title: Isaiah Chapter 3 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Isaiah chapter 3 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Isaiah Chapter 3 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Isaiah Chapter 3.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 3:1, what does the Lord take away from Jerusalem and Judah?
options: The stay and the staff, the whole stay of bread, and the whole stay of water
The mighty men and the judges
questions.correctAnswer: The stay and the staff, the whole stay of bread, and the whole stay of water
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:1 states that the Lord takes away the stay and the staff, the whole stay of bread, and the whole stay of water from Jerusalem and Judah.

questions.question: Who are listed as being taken away in Isaiah 3:2?
options: The mighty man, the man of war, the judge, the prophet, the prudent, and the ancient
questions.correctAnswer: The mighty man, the man of war, the judge, the prophet, the prudent, and the ancient
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:2 lists the mighty man, the man of war, the judge, the prophet, the prudent, and the ancient as those taken away.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT mentioned in Isaiah 3:3 as being removed?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:3 mentions the captain of fifty, the honourable man, the counsellor, the cunning artificer, and the eloquent orator, but not a mighty king.

questions.question: What unusual rulers does God say He will give in Isaiah 3:4?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:4 states that God will give children to be their princes and babes shall rule over them.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 3:5, how will people treat one another?
options: Oppressed, every one by another, and every one by his neighbour
questions.correctAnswer: Oppressed, every one by another, and every one by his neighbour
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:5 says the people shall be oppressed, every one by another, and every one by his neighbour.

questions.question: In Isaiah 3:6, what reason does a man give for asking his brother to be ruler?
options: Because he has clothing and can take charge of the ruin
Because he is wise and just
Because he is strong and mighty
Because he is a prophet and counsellor
questions.correctAnswer: Because he has clothing and can take charge of the ruin
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:6 records a man saying to his brother, 'Thou hast clothing, be thou our ruler, and let this ruin be under thy hand.'

questions.question: What does the man say he will NOT be in Isaiah 3:7?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:7 says he will swear, 'I will not be an healer; for in my house is neither bread nor clothing: make me not a ruler of the people.'

questions.question: Why is Jerusalem ruined and Judah fallen according to Isaiah 3:8?
options: Because their tongue and doings are against the LORD, to provoke the eyes of his glory
questions.correctAnswer: Because their tongue and doings are against the LORD, to provoke the eyes of his glory
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:8 states Jerusalem is ruined and Judah is fallen because their tongue and their doings are against the LORD, provoking His glory.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 3:9, how do the people treat their sin?
options: They declare their sin as Sodom and hide it not
They confess and repent of their sin
They keep their sin secret and hidden
They are unaware of their sin
questions.correctAnswer: They declare their sin as Sodom and hide it not
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:9 says their countenance witnesses against them and they declare their sin as Sodom, not hiding it.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 3:10 says that it shall be well with the righteous because they shall eat the fruit of their doings.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:10 states that it shall be well with the righteous because they shall eat the fruit of their doings.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 3:11 says that the wicked will be rewarded well for their hands.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:11 says woe unto the wicked; it shall be ill with him for the reward of his hands shall be given him, meaning punishment, not reward.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 3:12 states that children are oppressors and women rule over the people.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:12 says that children are their oppressors and women rule over them, causing them to err and destroying their paths.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 3:13 describes the LORD as standing to plead and judge the people.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:13 says the LORD standeth up to plead and standeth to judge the people, so this statement is True, but since two True and two False are needed, the correct answer must be True. Correction: This question's correctAnswer is 'True'.

questions.question: In Isaiah 3, which group is mentioned first as being taken away?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:2 lists the mighty man first among those taken away: 'The mighty man, and the man of war, the judge, the prophet, the prudent, and the ancient.'

questions.question: According to Isaiah 3:5, who behaves proudly against the ancient?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:5 says the child shall behave proudly against the ancient.

medium.title: Isaiah Chapter 3 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Isaiah Chapter 3 to real-life situations.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 3:10, what will happen to the righteous?
options: They shall eat the fruit of their doings
They shall be oppressed by others
questions.correctAnswer: They shall eat the fruit of their doings
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:10 states that the righteous will be well and will eat the fruit of their doings, indicating blessings come from their righteous actions.

questions.question: What consequence does Isaiah 3:11 say will come upon the wicked?
options: It shall be ill with him
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be ill with him
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:11 warns that the wicked will face ill consequences as a result of their actions, emphasizing divine justice.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 3:12 reveal about the leadership of the people?
options: Children and women rule over them
questions.correctAnswer: Children and women rule over them
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:12 describes a scenario where children oppress and women rule, illustrating a breakdown in proper leadership.

questions.question: What action is the LORD taking according to Isaiah 3:13?
options: Standing up to plead and judge the people
questions.correctAnswer: Standing up to plead and judge the people
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:13 shows the LORD actively engaging in judgment and pleading on behalf of justice among His people.

questions.question: What reason does Isaiah 3:14 give for the LORD entering into judgment with the leaders?
options: They have eaten up the vineyard and taken the spoil of the poor
They have led the people into battle
questions.correctAnswer: They have eaten up the vineyard and taken the spoil of the poor
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:14 states the leaders have exploited the poor by consuming what belongs to them, prompting divine judgment.

questions.question: What question does the Lord GOD of hosts ask in Isaiah 3:15?
options: What mean ye that ye beat my people to pieces?
Why do you build high towers?
Where is the temple of the LORD?
questions.correctAnswer: What mean ye that ye beat my people to pieces?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:15 records God's question about the harsh treatment of His people, emphasizing injustice against the poor.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 3:16, why does the LORD say He will punish the daughters of Zion?
options: Because they are haughty and walk with stretched forth necks and wanton eyes
questions.correctAnswer: Because they are haughty and walk with stretched forth necks and wanton eyes
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:16 describes the pride and vanity of the daughters of Zion as the cause of their coming punishment.

questions.question: What punishment does Isaiah 3:17 describe for the daughters of Zion?
options: The LORD will smite with a scab the crown of their heads
They will be exiled to a foreign land
They will be blessed with humility
questions.correctAnswer: The LORD will smite with a scab the crown of their heads
questions.explanation: Verse 17 foretells a physical affliction as a sign of judgment for their pride and vanity.

questions.question: Based on Isaiah 3:18-22, what will happen to the ornaments and apparel of the daughters of Zion?
options: They will be made more beautiful
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:18-22 lists various ornaments and apparel that the LORD will remove as part of the daughters of Zion's punishment.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 3:24 say will replace the sweet smell, girdle, and well-set hair?
options: Fragrance, a belt, and a crown
Peace, a robe, and long hair
questions.explanation: Verse 24 contrasts former beauty and adornments with decay and humiliation as divine judgment.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 3:25, what fate will come upon the men and mighty in war?
options: They shall fall by the sword
questions.correctAnswer: They shall fall by the sword
questions.explanation: Verse 25 declares the defeat and death of the strong warriors as part of the judgment.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 3:26 describe about the gates and the city in the day of judgment?
options: The gates shall lament and mourn; the city shall be desolate
The gates shall be strong and secure
The city shall celebrate with joy
The gates shall be open for all
questions.correctAnswer: The gates shall lament and mourn; the city shall be desolate
questions.explanation: Verse 26 portrays the city's desolation and mourning as a sign of judgment and loss.

questions.question: True or False: According to Isaiah 3:12, those who lead the people cause them to err and destroy the way of their paths.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:12 clearly states that the leaders cause the people to err and destroy the way of their paths, showing leadership failure.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 3:7 says a man will eagerly accept the role of ruler over the people because his house has plenty of bread and clothing.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:7 explains that a man will refuse to be ruler, saying he is not an healer and lacks bread and clothing, indicating reluctance to lead in difficult times.

questions.question: True or False: What Isaiah 3:10 promises for the righteous contrasts with the judgment pronounced on the wicked in the following verse, teaching about the outcomes of faithfulness and wickedness.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:10 and 3:11 together teach that the righteous will prosper and the wicked will suffer, highlighting the principle of divine justice.

hard.title: Isaiah Chapter 3 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Isaiah Chapter 3.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 3:19-23, which of the following was NOT listed among the ornaments to be taken away from the daughters of Zion?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:19-23 lists many ornaments such as chains, bracelets, rings, and glasses, but 'crowns' are not mentioned among these specific items.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 3:24 describe as the replacement for 'sweet smell'?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:24 explicitly states, 'instead of sweet smell there shall be stink,' indicating a reversal from something pleasant to something foul.

questions.question: Isaiah 3:25 speaks of the fate of the men and mighty in war. What is their fate?
options: They shall fall by the sword
questions.correctAnswer: They shall fall by the sword
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:25 clearly states that 'Thy men shall fall by the sword, and thy mighty in the war,' indicating death in battle.

questions.question: In Isaiah 3:26, what is said to happen to the gates of Jerusalem?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:26 states, 'And her gates shall lament and mourn; and she being desolate shall sit upon the ground,' emphasizing the city's desolation and sorrow.

questions.question: What literary device is prominently used in Isaiah 3:24 where contrasting images like 'sweet smell' and 'stink' are paired?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:24 uses antithesis by presenting direct opposites (sweet smell vs. stink) to emphasize judgment and reversal of fortunes.

questions.question: Which Hebrew word meaning 'to crumble' or 'fall apart' can be connected to the imagery of Jerusalem's desolation in Isaiah 3:26?
questions.explanation: The Hebrew root 'Shabar' (שָׁבַר) means 'to break' or 'crumble,' fitting the theme of Jerusalem's desolation in Isaiah 3:26 where the city sits desolate.

questions.question: Isaiah 3:16 mentions the daughters of Zion walking with 'stretched forth necks and wanton eyes.' What does this imagery primarily symbolize?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:16 explicitly says 'the daughters of Zion are haughty,' and the imagery of stretched necks and wanton eyes symbolizes arrogance and pride.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 3:12 indicates that women will rule over the people as a form of judgment.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:12 states, 'children are their oppressors, and women rule over them,' indicating an unusual and humiliating form of leadership as judgment.

questions.question: True or False: Isaiah 3:7 shows a man eagerly accepting the role of ruler over his people despite hardships.
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:7 shows the man refusing leadership, saying 'I will not be an healer; for in my house is neither bread nor clothing,' indicating unwillingness due to scarcity.

questions.question: Which other Bible passage echoes the theme of God removing leaders and causing societal collapse as in Isaiah 3:1-5?
questions.explanation: Jeremiah 5:31 similarly condemns corrupt leaders and judges whose failure brings ruin, paralleling Isaiah 3's theme of leadership removal and societal collapse.

questions.question: Isaiah 3:14-15 describes God entering judgment against the princes for their treatment of the poor. Which New Testament passage reflects a similar rebuke of oppressors?
questions.explanation: James 5:4 condemns the rich who oppress laborers, echoing Isaiah 3:14-15's condemnation of princes who exploit the poor.

questions.question: The phrase 'children shall rule over them' in Isaiah 3:4 is an example of what type of prophetic imagery?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:4 uses children ruling as a symbol of societal breakdown and reversal of normal order, not literal child rulers.

questions.question: Isaiah 3:17 says the Lord will 'smite with a scab the crown of the head' of the daughters of Zion. What is the significance of this expression in the ancient Near Eastern context?
options: A curse of physical disgrace and shame
questions.correctAnswer: A curse of physical disgrace and shame
questions.explanation: In ancient Near Eastern culture, skin diseases like scabs were seen as signs of divine punishment and public disgrace, as Isaiah 3:17 illustrates.

questions.question: Isaiah 3:20 lists 'the bonnets, and the ornaments of the legs, and the headbands.' What do these items collectively symbolize in the context of the chapter?
options: The vanity and pride of the daughters of Zion
The wealth and prosperity of Jerusalem
questions.correctAnswer: The vanity and pride of the daughters of Zion
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:20 lists these ornaments as part of the daughters of Zion's pride and vanity, which God intends to remove as judgment.

questions.question: How does the judgment described in Isaiah 3:24-26 foreshadow the suffering and desolation described in later prophetic books such as Lamentations?
options: Through the imagery of physical decay and mourning gates
By focusing on foreign conquest only
questions.correctAnswer: Through the imagery of physical decay and mourning gates
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:24-26's descriptions of baldness, sackcloth, and lamenting gates foreshadow the detailed suffering and desolation lamented in Lamentations.

theological.title: Isaiah Chapter 3 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Isaiah Chapter 3 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 3:1 indicate will be taken away from Jerusalem and Judah?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:1 specifically states that the Lord will take away 'the stay and the staff, the whole stay of bread, and the whole stay of water', indicating a removal of sustenance and support from the people.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 3:4, who will be given as princes?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:4 states, 'And I will give children to be their princes,' highlighting a time when the leaders will be inexperienced and immature.

questions.question: What behavior is described in Isaiah 3:5 regarding social relations?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:5 describes a society where 'the people shall be oppressed, every one by another,' indicating a breakdown of social order.

questions.question: In Isaiah 3:9, how do the people of Jerusalem declare their sins?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:9 states that they declare their sin 'as Sodom,' which implies an open and unabashed acknowledgment of their sinful actions.

questions.question: What will happen to the righteous according to Isaiah 3:10?
options: It shall be well with them
questions.correctAnswer: It shall be well with them
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:10 assures that 'it shall be well with him,' indicating that the righteous will receive blessings for their deeds.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 3:12 say about the leaders of the people?
options: They cause the people to err
questions.correctAnswer: They cause the people to err
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:12 states, 'they which lead thee cause thee to err,' highlighting how misguided leadership leads to the destruction of the community's paths.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is revealed in Isaiah 3:13 when the Lord pleads with the people?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:13 shows the Lord standing up to plead and judge the people, demonstrating His attribute of justice as He seeks to correct wrongs.

questions.question: What judgment will the Lord execute according to Isaiah 3:14?
options: Judgment on the ancients and princes
questions.correctAnswer: Judgment on the ancients and princes
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:14 indicates that the Lord 'will enter into judgment with the ancients of his people, and the princes thereof,' holding them accountable for their actions.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 3:24 say will replace beauty and adornment?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:24 prophesies that instead of beauty, there will be 'stink; and instead of a girdle a rent; and instead of well set hair baldness,' reflecting the consequences of sin.

questions.question: What is the fate of the men mentioned in Isaiah 3:25?
options: They shall fall by the sword
questions.correctAnswer: They shall fall by the sword
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:25 states that 'Thy men shall fall by the sword,' indicating impending destruction and loss in battle due to judgment.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 3:15 accuse the leaders of doing to the poor?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:15 questions, 'What mean ye that ye beat my people to pieces,' condemning the leaders for their harsh treatment of the vulnerable.

questions.question: How does Isaiah 3:16 describe the daughters of Zion?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:16 describes the daughters of Zion as 'haughty, and walk with stretched forth necks and wanton eyes,' indicating pride and moral decay.

questions.question: What does Isaiah 3:18 say the Lord will take away from the daughters of Zion?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:18 states that the Lord will take away 'the bravery of their tinkling ornaments,' indicating a stripping away of their superficial beauty and pride.

questions.question: What combined teaching do verses 8 and 9 convey about Jerusalem's state?
questions.explanation: Verses 8 and 9 reveal that 'Jerusalem is ruined, and Judah is fallen' due to their tongue and doings being against the Lord, highlighting their sinful state.

questions.question: According to Isaiah 3:10 and 11, what is the contrasting fate of the righteous and the wicked?
options: The righteous will be well and the wicked will suffer
questions.correctAnswer: The righteous will be well and the wicked will suffer
questions.explanation: Isaiah 3:10 assures that 'it shall be well with him' for the righteous while verse 11 pronounces woe upon the wicked, emphasizing the divine justice.
